title: Accelerating ReLU for MPC-Based Private Inference with a Communication-Efficient Sign Estimation
problem: ReLU activation functions are expensive to compute in Multi-Party Computation (MPC) based private inference systems due to their non-linear nature and high communication overhead between parties. Standard MPC protocols for ReLU require many rounds of secure computation.
motivation: Enabling efficient private neural network inference is critical for deploying machine learning on sensitive data without revealing information to other parties.
method: The approach uses a communication-efficient sign estimation technique to accelerate ReLU computation in MPC. By optimizing the protocol for computing the sign function (which determines whether ReLU outputs the input or zero), the method reduces communication rounds between parties. This likely combines approximation or novel cryptographic protocols to minimize message passing overhead.
key_novelty: Communication-efficient sign estimation protocol that reduces message rounds for ReLU computation in MPC-based private inference.
contributions: Communication-efficient sign estimation method for MPC
Accelerated ReLU protocol reducing inter-party communication
Improved efficiency for MPC-based private neural network inference systems
limitations: Limitations not discussed based on title-only analysis.
